highlights.title: Indeed Hiring Lab: 2026 Q3 US Tech Labor Market Update
highlights.summary: Tech job postings showed recent strength with wage growth in Q3 2026, but quit rates remain persistently low, suggesting workers are reluctant to change jobs despite improving conditions. Provides sector-level headcount and wage signal for tech workers.

highlights.title: Who Counts as Exposed? Measurement Choices in an Open, Re-estimable Index of Occupational AI Exposure
highlights.summary: An open, re-estimable task-level AI exposure index shows that varying two key design choices — context and calibration — produces materially different counts of which workers are classified as exposed, with important implications for workforce planning and policy.

highlights.title: Dull, Dirty, Dangerous? Working Conditions and the Limits of Occupational AI Exposure
highlights.summary: Across 754 US occupations, higher AI exposure is associated with lower 'dull, dirty, dangerous' condition scores under LLM-based measures, challenging the assumption that AI automation primarily relieves workers of undesirable tasks.

highlights.title: Strategic AI Underuse: Effort Incentives, Displacement Risk, and Organizational Responses
highlights.summary: A formal model shows workers who fear AI-driven displacement may rationally underuse AI tools, trading current earnings for job security — implying observed AI adoption rates in enterprises may systematically understate available productivity gains.

highlights.title: The Expanding Elite Premium: Task-Biased Technological Change and Higher Education Stratification in China
highlights.summary: Using three waves of Chinese household data (2013–2023), the paper finds that elite-university wage premia widened during early generative AI diffusion, consistent with task-biased technological change increasing returns to top-tier credentials.

highlights.title: Artificial Intelligence and Work: Evidence from the Portuguese Labor Market
highlights.summary: Thesis-level empirical study of the Portuguese labor market examines AI's realized effects on job replacement and productivity, providing European comparative evidence on displacement versus augmentation outcomes.

highlights.title: Artificial Intelligence Diffusion, Adaptive Human-Capital Transformation, and Unequal Development: Evidence from a 50-Country Panel
highlights.summary: A 229 country-year panel (50 countries) finds that AI capacity, human-capital transformation, and labor-market structure jointly predict unequal development outcomes, with high-skill labor markets capturing most AI-related gains.

highlights.title: Technology Budgets, Innovations and Labor Market Dynamics: Evidence from OECD Countries
highlights.summary: Using Dynamic Common Correlated Effects on 24 OECD countries (2007–2024), R&D-proxied technology budgets are linked to unemployment dynamics, providing multi-country evidence on how technology investment reshapes labor demand.

highlights.title: Indeed Hiring Lab: October 2026 Jobs Report: Some Tarnish Beneath the Headline Shine
highlights.summary: Indeed Hiring Lab's read of the October 2026 BLS jobs report finds headline gains masking real difficulty for unemployed workers seeking re-entry, with job-finding conditions described as challenging for those outside current employment.

highlights.title: Indeed Hiring Lab: September 2026 JOLTS Report: Eerily Quiet
highlights.summary: September 2026 JOLTS data show unusually low labor market churn — quits, hires, and layoffs all subdued — signaling a 'wait and see' labor market with limited worker mobility.

highlights.title: Indeed Hiring Lab: 2026 Q3 US Business-to-Business Labor Market Update
highlights.summary: B2B sector job postings were up year-over-year in most categories in Q3 2026, suggesting relative resilience in professional services and enterprise-facing roles despite broader automation headwinds.

highlights.title: Beyond AI Productivity: Enterprise AI Systems, Human–AI Responsibility, and the Future of Work
highlights.summary: A U.S.-focused review finds enterprise AI assistants have task-dependent productivity effects but that public evidence does not identify an independent financial return or a complete chain from AI cost to verified workforce outcomes.

highlights.title: Will AI Growth Reach the Developing World?
highlights.summary: A growth model of developed and developing economies finds that whether AI services substitute for or complement different labor inputs determines whether AI-driven growth in rich countries widens or narrows global wage and income gaps.

highlights.title: Indeed Hiring Lab: 2026 Q3 US Transportation Labor Market Update
highlights.summary: Three of four transportation sub-categories posted year-over-year job posting gains in Q3 2026, providing sector-level evidence relevant to physical automation displacement forecasts.

highlights.title: Revelio Labs: RPLS Jobs Report — Workforce Research Newsroom
highlights.summary: Revelio Labs' November RPLS monthly release covers realized workforce transitions using linked employer-employee data, offering timely private-sector job flow evidence to complement BLS official series.

themes: Tech labor market stabilizing but workers staying put — low quits and subdued churn dominate Q3 2026 readings
AI exposure measurement under scrutiny — new methodological work shows index design choices materially change which workers count as at risk
Strategic AI underuse and elite skill premiums emerging as supply-side responses to displacement anxiety
